deities: Goddess Burhi - primordial deity later sanskritised as Goddess Durga/Kali

history.period: 1794 CE (established at Jorhat; idol brought from the Jaintia hills earlier)
history.summary: Shakta temple on Dewal Road in Jorhat city, originally dedicated to the primordial deity Burhi and later sanskritised to goddess Durga. The idol was brought from the Jaintia hills of Meghalaya into the Ahom kingdom by Ahom king Rudra Singha; when Ahom king Gaurinath Singha shifted the capital from Rangpur to Jorhat, the Burhi Gosani Devalaya was established at Jorhat in 1794. (One secondary source says the temple and priest were first established at Rangpur/Sivasagar in 1714.) The annual Durga Puja is the temple's main event. Published coordinates: 26 deg 45'32"N 94 deg 12'53"E. FLAG: MakeMyTrip describes this site as an 18th-century temple dedicated to Lord Shiva built by Rajeshwar Singha - this conflicts with the Shakta/Burhi tradition documented by Wikipedia, temple directories and the IGNCA; deity and founder details should be verified locally before publication.

name: Burigosain Devalay (Buri Gossain Temple)
town_description: Jorhat is the cultural and commercial centre of Upper Assam, often called the Tea Capital of India for the research institutes and tea estates around it. It was the last capital of the Ahom kingdom (from 1794), and remains a hub of the Ekasarana Neo-Vaishnavite tradition, with historic namghars, maidams and temples in and around the city.

travel.airport: Rowriah (Jorhat) Airport is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Jorhat Town Railway Station is the nearest major railway station.
travel.road: On Dewal Road in central Jorhat; easily reached by auto-rickshaw or taxi within the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October-November during Durga Puja, the temple's main annual event.
